issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares the lectureName attribute as type int (Lecture -lectureName: int), but the rest of the exercise (example toString output, the intended constructor and methods, and the solution implementation) treat lectureName as a String. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected type for lectureName and lead them to implement the attribute incorrectly (as an int) which will not work with the toString example or with getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents().
issues.suggested_fix: Correct the UML (and any explicit type mentions) in the problem statement to declare lectureName as a String (lectureName: String), so it matches the example toString, the described behavior, and the solution implementation. This will remove ambiguity for students when they add the attribute and constructor in the template.
